title: His favorite and unreleased recordings as a leader
summary: Hug picks Golden Crest, drum-and-piano, and Circle sessions, and an unreleased Golliwog album covering many pianists' styles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you want to go back and play? Left off, let's see, we're talking about ragtime, this was kind of shifted a bit. You made many recordings in the past years. Do you have any sessions that you would point out to as being your favorite or your better sessions that you feel are more representative of your playing?

Yeah, the sessions that I made that are better representative are on Golden Crest label with, it's under the title of Rags and Blues. And then, of course, the records that I made with Ray Badouk, I think, on drums, that was just drum and piano solos, you know, when I made Little Rock Getaway. I made an album on Circle back in 1950 that was very good, technically, you know, I mean, from a recording standpoint and all.
Have you ever recorded anything which shows the broader scope of your playing? I just heard you're playing, was it, was it that Melchor May tune, was it? What were you just doing?
Cast Your Fate to the Wind?

Yeah, and then I've heard you do several other things that I think are excellent in that same vein, like Taste of Honey. Has this phase of your musical personality ever been recorded accurately, you think?

No, I don't believe accurately. I've tried to put it across on some of the recordings. The album that I made here at the Gollywog that has never been released, I think, contains more of this than anything else that I've ever done. But it's been most unfortunate that it's never been released. And in this album, I attempted more styles, different things that I've ever done before. In fact, I did a lot of Royal Heinz, Teddy Wilson, George Shearing, Jess Stacey, Errol Garner. In fact, I tried to cover practically every pianist of any importance that I could ever think of.
